Finding_Text: Quarterly user access reviews were not performed for the cloud production environment during Q2.
Orphaned user accounts discovered belonging to 14 terminated employees still active in Active Directory.
Developers granted permanent administrator and root privileges on production database instances.
Lack of documented managerial approval tickets for elevated access rights granted to temporary contractors.
Principle of least privilege violated with 22 team members assigned excessive superuser roles.
Separation of duties conflict: the same engineering user can write code, approve pull requests, and deploy.
Offboarding workflow failed to deprovision access rights for 5 departing contractors within 24 hours.
Generic shared administrator login utilized by multiple shift engineers without individual attribution.
Role-based access control (RBAC) definitions have not been reviewed or updated following reorganization.
Privilege creep observed: internal transferred employees retained historical access rights to payroll systems.
Emergency break-glass administrative access accounts were activated without subsequent log review or justification.
Third-party support team was assigned persistent administrative rights instead of time-limited access.
User access review was conducted without manager sign-off or documented revocation records.
System administrator accounts permitted wildcard IAM policy permissions (Action: * on Resource: *).
Service accounts utilized for internal microservice communication possessed unnecessary global admin rights.
Inactive user accounts with no login activity for over 180 days were not automatically disabled.
Contractor access agreements lacked defined expiration dates, resulting in indefinite active status.
Privileged access management (PAM) solution not enforced for accessing production bastion hosts.
Access rights to sensitive customer billing records granted without documented business justification.
Audit trail revealed 8 users whose access rights exceeded their documented job roles.
SCIM automated user deprovisioning failed between HRIS software and SaaS applications.
Production SSH access granted to all engineering staff without role restriction or ticketing.
Absence of formal entitlement re-certification process for users with privileged access rights.
Default administrative accounts (admin, sa, root) remained active with default access rights.
Just-in-time (JIT) access requests were automatically approved without peer or supervisor authorization.
Critical cloud service provider SOC 2 Type II report expired 11 months ago without renewed review.
Procurement onboarded a new SaaS vendor without completing a third-party security risk assessment.
Vendor master contract lacks a mandatory 72-hour security incident notification SLA requirement.
Third-party supplier risk register is not maintained to track external vendor compliance posture.
No formal Data Processing Addendum (DPA) signed with marketing SaaS supplier processing customer emails.
Annual vendor security re-assessment was not performed for Tier-1 suppliers hosting corporate data.
Vendor contracts fail to include right-to-audit clauses or certified data sanitization requirements.
Sub-processor list for critical payment vendor was not reviewed prior to contract renewal.
Third-party consulting firm had unmonitored site-to-site access without signed confidentiality agreements.
Absence of documented vendor tiering criteria to categorize suppliers based on data risk and criticality.
SaaS vendor security questionnaire completed with multiple non-compliant answers without risk acceptance.
Vendor offboarding procedure not executed: terminated supplier retained remote connectivity to internal portals.
Bridge letters not requested from vendors operating on outdated SOC 2 observation periods.
Critical infrastructure supplier failed to provide evidence of annual disaster recovery tabletop testing.
Third-party vendor background verification checks for offshore developers were not verified by management.
Supplier security SLAs for critical vulnerability remediation were omitted from master service agreements.
New cloud vendor integrated into core workflow without legal or information security committee sign-off.
Vendor access to internal customer databases provisioned without dedicated third-party NDA on file.
Lack of continuous monitoring for third-party vendor security ratings and public breach notifications.
Supply chain risk assessment failed to identify fourth-party hosting dependencies for critical payment processor.
Supplier compliance tracking does not verify whether third parties maintain active ISO 27001 certifications.
Third-party vendor data retention periods exceed agreed contractual limits without remediation.
Vendor risk management program does not evaluate supplier business continuity or financial solvency.
Supplier exit strategy and transition runbooks not documented for Tier-1 mission-critical vendors.
Security team omitted SIG Lite questionnaire reviews for external managed service providers.
Remote employee laptops discovered operating without FileVault or BitLocker full-disk encryption.
Mobile Device Management (MDM) enrollment agent uninstalled on 8 company-issued MacBooks.
Endpoint screen lock auto-lock timeout was disabled across 15 developer desktop computers.
Personal non-company laptops (BYOD) accessing internal repositories without endpoint security controls.
USB mass storage ports not restricted, allowing employees to connect unencrypted external thumb drives.
Missing Endpoint Detection and Response (EDR) agent on newly provisioned developer workstations.
Local administrative rights enabled on standard business laptops allowing unauthorized software installation.
Remote wipe command failed on lost company smartphone due to expired MDM management certificates.
Corporate laptops do not enforce host-based personal firewalls to block unauthorized incoming connections.
Automated third-party application patch management not configured for desktop browsers and tools.
Endpoint security agent tamper protection disabled by users to execute unauthorized local scripts.
Workstation baseline security configurations not formally documented or enforced across remote workers.
Stolen employee laptop lacked hardware TPM chip encryption for securing local credentials.
Corporate endpoints permitted automatic connection to unsecured public Wi-Fi networks without VPN.
Bluetooth file sharing enabled on corporate workstations without restriction or security logging.
Endpoint inventory database out of sync with active workstation fleet by more than 20% discrepancy.
Antivirus virus definitions and signature updates failing to sync on 12 remote laptops for over 30 days.
Employee laptops allowed installation of peer-to-peer file sharing and torrent applications.
Lost laptop incident reported 5 days late due to lack of employee device security awareness training.
MDM profile does not enforce minimum 8-character PIN passcode on company-managed mobile smartphones.
Employee workstations permitted boots from external unverified USB drives via unlocked BIOS.
Decommissioned employee laptops disposed of without serialized certificates of hard drive destruction.
Endpoint DLP software disabled on engineering laptops allowing unrestricted clipboard and file exports.
Workstations permitted execution of unsigned binaries and unapproved scripts in user temp directories.
Operating system updates postponed indefinitely by users due to lack of enforced MDM restart policies.
Cloud infrastructure management console accessed via single-factor password without MFA enforcement.
Employee VPN allows authentication via insecure SMS text one-time passcodes vulnerable to SIM swapping.
Password policy permits weak 8-character passwords without complexity or dictionary breach validation.
Administrative login portals lack account lockout mechanisms after consecutive failed authentication attempts.
Service accounts utilize static passwords that have not been rotated or changed in over 12 months.
Internal developer dashboard login does not integrate with central Okta SSO and uses local credentials.
Web user session tokens remain valid indefinitely after browser closure due to missing session timeout.
Production server SSH access permits password-based login rather than requiring SSH key authentication.
Phishing-resistant WebAuthn or FIDO2 hardware MFA tokens not enforced for administrative superusers.
Self-service password reset workflow relies exclusively on easily guessed security challenge questions.
MFA exemption granted to executive accounts without documented expiration dates or compensatory controls.
API authentication relies on basic HTTP authentication headers transmitting cleartext credentials.
Simultaneous concurrent user logins from geographically impossible locations not flagged by auth system.
Customer login portal lacks rate limiting or CAPTCHA protection against automated credential stuffing.
Default administrative factory passwords remained unchanged on production network switches.
Remember Me authentication cookies persist login state across untrusted devices for 90 days.
Authentication server logs do not record source IP addresses or failed login attempt telemetry.
Microservices authenticate using unencrypted static API bearer tokens without JWT signature verification.
Single sign-on (SSO) SAML assertion tokens accepted without verifying digital signature validity.
Root AWS account login does not have a physical hardware MFA token configured in executive safe.
Password history check not enforced, allowing users to alternate between 2 previous passwords.
OAuth 2.0 authorization code flow implemented without PKCE protection against authorization code injection.
Session revocation does not terminate active user sessions across all connected mobile and web devices.
Privileged admin portal allows remember password browser auto-fill without re-authentication prompt.
Multi-factor authentication challenge prompt suppressed for trusted IP ranges that included public Wi-Fi.
Production web servers running unpatched OpenSSL library with known critical vulnerability (CVE-2023-3817).
Critical security patch for Linux kernel vulnerability not deployed after 45 days, breaching 14-day SLA.
Monthly automated vulnerability scanning is not configured for customer-facing Kubernetes production nodes.
Container base images in production registry contain 8 Critical and 15 High CVEs according to scan reports.
Third-party penetration testing identified unpatched log4j remote code execution vulnerability on analytics worker.
Vulnerability management policy lacks a formal SLA timeline for remediating Low and Medium vulnerabilities.
Production server running deprecated PHP runtime reaching official vendor end-of-life without updates.
Security operations team does not subscribe to threat intelligence advisories or zero-day vulnerability alerts.
External attack surface scanner identified exposed Apache server disclosing outdated version banners.
DevOps team deployed staging containers to production without executing automated vulnerability gate checks.
High severity vulnerability in internal DNS server identified during audit remains unpatched for 75 days.
Lack of automated patch management software across on-premises test lab infrastructure.
Authenticated vulnerability scanner credentials expired, causing weekly scans to fail silently for 2 months.
Remediation verification scans are not performed after patching to confirm vulnerability resolution.
Legacy database operating system has not received security patches since vendor end-of-support in 2022.
Container Dockerfile configurations do not pin package versions, causing unpredictable vulnerability regressions.
No vulnerability tracking ticket created for critical zero-day exploit announced in national CVE database.
Server AMI golden images used for auto-scaling groups have not been patched or rebuilt in 150 days.
Penetration test findings from previous annual audit were not remediated within the agreed 90-day window.
Vulnerability scanning excluded external APIs and customer portal subdomains from audit scope.
Critical zero-day vulnerability patch released by vendor was not evaluated or tested within 48 hours.
Lack of formal patch exception logging mechanism for legacy systems that cannot be patched immediately.
Production container registry lacks automated continuous vulnerability scanning upon image push.
Firmware security updates have not been applied to enterprise edge routing hardware for over 2 years.
Static vulnerability reports sent via email instead of being tracked in an automated ticketing workflow.
AWS S3 bucket hosting confidential customer files configured with public read access enabled to internet.
Application debug logs contain unmasked customer credit card numbers and plain social security numbers.
Production customer personally identifiable information (PII) replicated to unencrypted test environment.
Lack of egress filtering or data loss prevention (DLP) controls on corporate email allowing bulk data export.
Employee exported 50,000 customer contact records to personal cloud storage without DLP alert.
Sensitive tenant database records stored in world-readable temporary directory on staging server.
Public git repository accidentally committed customer identity verification documents and passports.
Data loss prevention (DLP) agent running in monitor-only mode and not actively blocking data exfiltration.
Contractor downloaded 10GB of customer financial records to unencrypted personal USB drive without block.
API responses return complete customer profile records including unredacted tax IDs to browser frontend.
Absence of automated data classification labeling across cloud object stores holding confidential data.
Clipboard copying and screenshots of sensitive customer records permitted during remote virtual desktop sessions.
Database snapshots containing customer personal data shared across AWS accounts without DLP authorization.
Customer support ticket system attachments containing medical records accessible via unauthenticated URLs.
Outbound web proxy does not inspect or block data leakage patterns matching credit card or IBAN numbers.
Data retention policy not enforced, allowing 6-year-old customer personal data to linger on test servers.
Insecure direct object reference (IDOR) allowed external users to enumerate and download customer contracts.
Unrestricted file upload mechanism allowed external data exfiltration via reverse shell upload.
Corporate cloud storage folders shared publicly with 'Anyone with the link can view' permissions.
Production database query results containing customer names exported to unmonitored Slack channels.
Lack of endpoint DLP controls to prevent printing or local downloading of proprietary patent documents.
Customer PII exposed in unredacted URL query parameters captured in third-party analytics trackers.
Marketing team forwarded unencrypted customer email database lists to third-party survey provider.
Confidential source code repositories cloned to personal laptops without data loss prevention safeguards.
Egress bandwidth anomaly indicating 500GB outbound data transfer to unknown IP was not alerted by DLP.
PostgreSQL database automated backups failed silently for 14 consecutive days without engineer alerts.
Annual disaster recovery backup restoration drill was not conducted during the past 12 months.
Database backup snapshots are stored in the same geographic region as production, vulnerable to regional outage.
Database restoration test revealed corrupted transaction logs resulting in unrecoverable 48-hour data loss.
Backup storage buckets do not have Object Lock or write-once-read-many (WORM) ransomware protection.
Absence of automated monitoring alerts notifying team when scheduled nightly backup jobs fail to execute.
Recovery Time Objective (RTO) and Recovery Point Objective (RPO) metrics are not documented or tested.
Offsite tape and cold storage backups have not undergone integrity verification or restore tests in 2 years.
Kubernetes cluster state and etcd configuration backups are not scheduled or retained automatically.
Backup retention policy does not satisfy statutory 7-year regulatory financial record keeping mandates.
Manual database dump process used instead of automated point-in-time recovery (PITR) backup snapshots.
Disaster recovery plan contains obsolete server hostnames and outdated operational restoration procedures.
Secondary disaster recovery cloud site lacks sufficient compute capacity to handle production failover.
Virtual machine snapshot restoration procedure failed during simulated disaster recovery exercise.
Backup operator permissions granted to standard developers allowing unauthorized manual snapshot deletion.
Differential backup strategy not documented, leading to confusion during multi-step database restore trial.
Critical customer database excluded from daily automated backup synchronization schedule.
Database backup replication across secondary cloud availability zones was disabled without approval.
Disaster recovery communication tree contains contact details for former employees who left the firm.
Cold backup archives stored on unencrypted external hard drives without physical chain of custody.
Database backup job exceeded allocated maintenance window, causing production API timeouts.
No formal verification performed to ensure database backups are free from ransomware encryption before restore.
Application state and configuration files excluded from backup runbook, preventing full system rebuild.
Disaster recovery failover simulation revealed that secondary DNS records were improperly configured.
Backup deletion protection was not configured, allowing accidental removal of critical monthly snapshots.
Production database security group allows unrestricted inbound network traffic from 0.0.0.0/0 on port 5432.
SSH administrative port 22 open directly to the public internet across multiple cloud compute instances.
Internal office network lacks network segmentation between guest Wi-Fi and production server subnets.
Virtual Private Cloud (VPC) lacks flow logging enabled for network traffic analysis and intrusion detection.
Web Application Firewall (WAF) is unconfigured on the public API gateway, leaving endpoints exposed.
Internal microservices communicate across unsegmented network without network boundary isolation.
Intrusion Detection System (IDS) alerts disabled due to alert fatigue without tuning rule thresholds.
Default route table directs all private subnet database traffic through an internet gateway.
Production Kubernetes nodes share common flat subnet with public-facing ingress load balancers.
Network architecture diagram has not been updated following the deployment of new European cloud VPC.
Unrestricted egress firewall rules permit compromised production instances to connect to arbitrary IPs.
Remote Desktop Protocol (RDP) port 3389 discovered open to external internet on staging Windows server.
VPC peering connection configured without security group route filtering between prod and staging.
DNS zone transfers permitted from external unauthorized nameservers without access control.
Lack of Network Access Control Lists (NACLs) to provide packet filtering at subnet boundaries.
Production web servers lack DDoS mitigation protection against volumetric network flood attacks.
Bastion jump host placed in public subnet without IP whitelisting restricting inbound administrative access.
Internal network switches operate with default unencrypted SNMP community strings (public and private).
Demilitarized Zone (DMZ) architecture not implemented to isolate internet-facing services from database.
Network perimeter penetration test identified open Telnet and FTP ports on legacy border gateway.
Cloud security groups contain unused stale rules permitting ingress from deprecated office IP ranges.
Split-tunneling permitted on remote workforce VPN without corporate network traffic inspection.
Network intrusion prevention system (NIPS) signatures out of date by more than 90 days.
Lack of ingress rate limiting on public API endpoints resulting in denial of service vulnerability.
Internal corporate DNS servers resolve external malicious domains without protective DNS filtering.
Production database storage volumes stored without AWS KMS AES-256 customer-managed key encryption at rest.
Web server SSL/TLS configuration supports deprecated TLS 1.0 and TLS 1.1 protocols and weak CBC ciphers.
Cryptographic master encryption keys stored in plaintext configuration files inside application code.
Internal credit card tokenization service utilizes obsolete 3DES cipher rather than modern AES-256-GCM.
Root certificate authority and intermediate TLS signing keys lack automated annual rotation schedules.
Customer passwords stored in database using weak MD5 and SHA-1 hashing algorithms without salt.
Application secrets and API private keys hardcoded in plaintext within Docker container environment vars.
Database connection strings transmit credentials over unencrypted cleartext database protocols.
Lack of hardware security module (HSM) or dedicated KMS key management policy governing key lifecycle.
Cryptographic keys utilized for both encryption and digital signing, violating key separation principles.
Expired SSL/TLS certificate on customer payment portal caused browser security warnings for 36 hours.
Data-at-rest encryption disabled on Elasticsearch analytics cluster containing customer search queries.
Symmetric encryption keys shared across all tenant environments rather than using isolated per-tenant keys.
Weak RSA 1024-bit key pairs used for internal server identity certificates instead of modern 2048-bit keys.
Cryptographic initialization vectors (IV) statically reused across multiple encryption operations in cipher.
Key custodian procedures not documented for emergency revocation of compromised TLS wildcard certs.
Cleartext HTTP traffic allowed on customer registration endpoint without mandatory HTTPS redirect.
Lack of envelope encryption for large binary customer document attachments stored in object storage.
Cryptographic salt length for bcrypt password hashing algorithm set below the minimum 12-round threshold.
S3 bucket storage encryption uses default Amazon S3 keys rather than customer-controlled KMS keys.
Public API accepts SSL certificates signed by untrusted or expired internal root certificates.
Database field-level encryption not applied to sensitive columns storing taxpayer identification numbers.
Cryptographic key backup copies stored in unencrypted S3 bucket without KMS envelope protection.
Production web servers do not enforce HTTP Strict Transport Security (HSTS) response headers.
Private PGP decryption keys stored on shared network drive without passphrase protection.
Production payment microservice vulnerable to SQL injection due to unsanitized raw string query concat.
Hardcoded GitHub personal access token and AWS secret access key discovered in git commit history.
CI/CD build pipeline does not enforce automated static application security testing (SAST) before merge.
Cross-site scripting (XSS) vulnerability identified in customer portal dashboard search input field.
Pull request merged to production main branch without required independent peer code review sign-off.
Application backend deserializes untrusted user JSON payloads without input schema validation checks.
Software bill of materials (SBOM) and software dependency scanning (SCA) missing from build automation.
Insecure direct object reference (IDOR) flaw allows users to manipulate user_id parameters in code.
Development and testing libraries (e.g., debug console, mock endpoints) inadvertently deployed in build.
Absence of secure coding training for engineering staff covering OWASP Top 10 web vulnerabilities.
Server-side request forgery (SSRF) flaw in document conversion service allows access to cloud metadata.
Cross-site request forgery (CSRF) tokens not validated on state-changing administrative POST endpoints.
Code repository branch protection rules disabled, allowing developers to push directly to production main.
Application displays detailed verbose stack traces and database schema errors directly to end users.
File upload endpoint allows execution of arbitrary executable scripts without file extension filtering.
Security unit tests and automated regression test suites are not integrated into pull request checks.
Third-party JavaScript libraries loaded from external CDNs without Subresource Integrity (SRI) hashes.
Lack of automated pre-commit secret detection hooks to prevent developers from committing credentials.
Command injection vulnerability in server-side reporting script executing unvalidated shell commands.
XML external entity (XXE) injection flaw discovered in XML parsing module used for invoice processing.
Application source code repository accessible to all corporate employees without team-based restrictions.
Open redirect vulnerability in login callback handler allowing redirection to untrusted external URLs.
Dynamic code evaluation (eval()) used in production JavaScript to parse configuration objects.
Lack of Content Security Policy (CSP) headers to prevent execution of unauthorized inline scripts.
Software development lifecycle (SDLC) policy lacks mandatory threat modeling for new feature releases.
